One slice-scheme proof for the single-piece and joint-slice lifts

Notes L.16q-r built the joint-slice lift by copying the single-piece lift at
every level (line cell, affine cell, spectrum cover, core and global lift),
with the slice providers replaced by joint covers. The copies differ in one
step, on a dense set of anchors:
- the single lift applies a local piece provider to the first section, then
  to the second inside its agreement set;
- the joint lift covers both sections at once (joint_cover_on).

- SliceScheme (Proofs16SinglePieceSections) packages that step: a slice
  condition SL, the width wid θ L and density dens θ of its two-section box,
  with wid_mono and dens_pos. SliceScheme.congr holds for every scheme by
  funext. It has two instances:
  - localPieceScheme: providers, one section after the other; width
    w (c θ) (w θ L), density c (c θ);
  - jointSliceScheme (Proofs16JointSliceCell): a joint cover over Bool at
    θ/4; width ⌈L^(Eb(θ/4)²)⌉, density (θ - θ/2)/Qb(θ/4)².
- Each level is proved once, for any scheme:
  - single_piece_on_line_cell_of_scheme;
  - single_piece_on_affine_cell_of_scheme;
  - single_piece_of_spectrum_cover_for_scheme;
  - single_piece_lift_core_rem_scheme;
  - single_piece_lift_global_cover_scheme, which takes the map from a
    translated face cover of a slice to its slice condition (hof).
- The printed single-piece lemmas are the instances at localPieceScheme, and
  single_piece_lift_global_cover_with_joint is the instance at
  jointSliceScheme. All statements are unchanged.
- The joint chain's intermediate instances had no users and are deleted:
  - the joint line-cell, affine-cell, spectrum-cover and core lemmas;
  - jointSliceWidth_mono, which is now wid_mono.

  Proofs16JointSliceSpectrum and Proofs16JointSliceCore become empty and
  are removed. Proofs16JointSliceGlobal imports Proofs16JointSliceCell.
- The production-handoff list in FORMALIZATION_STATUS.txt and the generator
  README record the fold.

Inline 11 longer private helpers as documented have blocks

used at a whole-line `have h := L args` / `exact L args`, where
inlining stays idiomatic. The rest are used inside expressions. This

- only `private` lemmas: public single-use theorems such as

tactics spliced in at an `exact`), and its docstring is kept as `--`
